claim: Every item in the catalog is charged 25 cents a day when it is late, no fee goes above 10.00, and an item returned on its due date costs nothing.
why: The README says 25 cents a day for everything, but rates.py doubles the base rate for the disc format, and D300 is the only disc, so it is charged 50 cents a day and the first part is false. The cap and the on-time rule both hold, which makes the claim look right to anyone who trusts the README and the base rate. The false part sits in a small multiplier table in a helper, not in the catalog or the fee function.

deciding.note: D300 is a disc and is charged 50 cents a day through the multiplier in rates.py

root.claim: Every item is charged 25 cents a day, the fee is capped at 10.00, and an on-time return costs nothing.

atoms.claim: Every item in the catalog is charged 25 cents a day when late.
atoms.evidence: rates.py daily_rate multiplies BASE_RATE 0.25 by MULTIPLIER for the disc format, and catalog.py marks D300 as disc, so D300 is charged 50 cents a day; report.py shows D300 ten days late costs 5.00, not 2.50.
fees.py late_fee takes min(days * rate, MAX_FEE) with MAX_FEE 10.00; M200 two months late prints 10.00.

atoms.claim: An item returned on its due date costs nothing.
atoms.evidence: days_late returns max(0, 0) = 0; B100 returned on its due date prints 0.00.
